speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what are the specific measures to ensure widespread implementation of the new salary guidelines for the community care sector; (b) what are the incentives in place to encourage community care institutions to comply with the guidelines; (c) how will the Ministry conduct the monitoring of salaries; and (d) what factors will be considered when reviewing the guidelines.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the rationale for the existence of separate salary guidelines for the community care sector issued by the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Social and Family Development through the National Council of Social Service; and (b) whether the Ministries will collaborate to develop a unified set of salary guidelines to avoid confusion within the community care sector and to ensure consistency and clarity for both employers and employees.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the projected increase in operational costs for community care institutions to adopt the new salary guidelines; (b) how will institutions run by voluntary welfare organisations with a tight budget be affected; (c) whether the increase in service costs will be passed on to beneficiaries; (d) whether the Ministry will help institutions to subsidise salary increments; and (e) what support will be provided to help institutions to attract and retain staff.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Through in-depth engagement sessions with Community Care Organisations (CCOs), the Ministry of Health (MOH) provides them with guidance on implementation, such as establishing the appropriate banding of staff and salaries.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In reviewing the guidelines, we will consider salary movements in relevant labour markets.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Higher salaries will lead to higher operating costs for all CCOs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Beyond ensuring that salaries in the community care sector are competitive, MOH and our agencies support the CCOs to ensure that their workforce is future-ready through training and development programmes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have also worked with CCOs to redesign job roles to elevate community care careers and improve their attractiveness.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I declare that I am an advisor to the Healthcare Services Employees' Union (HSEU).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How are the salaries in the community compared to the acute hospitals and is there a significant difference?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If so, will the pay alone be a significant factor in drawing manpower either way to institutions or to the community?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be any effect on our priorities in staffing the community hospitals or the hospitals in the acute sector?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To this end, what are the Ministry's plans to address other factors influencing staff satisfaction and retention, such as career progression, opportunities or mental health support?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With regards to the public healthcare institutions (PHIs), as the Member is an advisor to the HSEU, he would then be aware that the PHIs already have prevailing collective agreements signed with HSEU.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These collective agreements include information on salary ranges and other information such as leave benefits.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that can be accessed through the HSEU's website and that provides a comparison with the CCOs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Salary guidelines are published for purposes of transparency and clarity to jobseekers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is intended to encourage them to see the benefits and salaries, but CCOs also have to do their part.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They also have to attract and retain their staff.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For PHIs, MOH also does the same thing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We work with them to regularly monitor and review their salaries to keep it competitive against the market.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As you would know, our manpower costs already account for 50% of our expenses.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This means that we are actually increasing the costs as we increase the services, and Government expenditure is expected to go up.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think all parties have to play a part in this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Already as it stands, we are looking at an increase and this increase has been growing in tandem with the healthcare demands.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Member had also asked about the efforts to attract and retain workers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think the Member had also filed a written Parliamentary Question, which is also scheduled for answer today, in relation to this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As mentioned earlier, we also look at training and development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There is different funding support for a suite of initiatives to attract, develop and retain workers in the community care sector.
